title: Continuous coefficient encoding for the exact ambient derived scalar adjunction
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed field extension, and let $A=\mathcal O_E$ with uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a noetherian scheme, and use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_T$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], $A_T(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$. Identify $B_T$ with $A_T$ by the canonical quotient projections, and use the ring map $B_T\to E_T$ given by this identification followed by postcomposition with $A\hookrightarrow E$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Let $A_T^c=p_T^*C(-,A)$ and $E_T^c=p_T^*C(-,E)$ be the internal coefficient rings [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], with their actual inclusion, and let $\Phi_A,\Phi_E$ be the specified internal-to-sectionwise module encodings [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding]. Write $D(\Phi_A),D(\Phi_E)$ for their termwise derived equivalences, and $Q$ for localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Ordinary scalar extension $E_T\otimes_{B_T}-$ and restriction of scalars are additive and exact; the same holds in internal modules. The actual unbounded derived functor $F=E_T\otimes^L_{B_T}-$ is triangulated with its termwise shift comparison, and every complex $K$ computes it: $F(QK)\cong Q(E_T\otimes_{B_T}K)$, naturally in $K$. There is a natural isomorphism of derived functors $D(\Phi_E)\circ(E_T^c\otimes^L_{A_T^c}-)\cong F\circ D(\Phi_A)$, identifying the actual coefficient inclusion and its ordinary scalar-extension comparison, with the termwise comparison on complexes. The functor $F$ is left adjoint to the exact termwise derived restriction $U$. Under the displayed factorization isomorphisms, its unit on every representing complex is $\eta_{QK}=Q(K\to U(E_T\otimes_{B_T}K))$, where the chain map sends each local section $m$ to $1\otimes m$. The same normalization holds under the specified internal encodings. No boundedness, constructibility or completeness hypothesis is imposed on $K$.

proof.text: Use chartComparison_naturality and the specified coefficient equalities lisseIntegerSheaf_eq and lisseFieldSheaf_eq. The equality lisseScalar_square identifies the two actual inclusions. Restriction along the inverse charts, sectionModuleComapIso, and identity linear maps for ring-isomorphism transport give a restriction comparison whose map on every section is the identity. The private helpers ringRestriction, ringIsoRestriction and spectralRestriction implement these three operations without choosing a new encoding.

Reuse the existing proved ordinaryAdjunction_exists and reductionUnit_apply of AdicCoefficientDatum. These apply sheafRingCoefficientOrdinaryAdjunction to the fixed reductionChange presentation and evaluate at the identity to give unit m ↦ 1 tensor m. Take the inverse mate of the restriction comparison across this adjunction and extendRestrictAdjunction. Since both vertical functors are equivalences, the mate is invertible (apply the equivalence mate theorem to opposite categories). Its mate-unit identity gives exactly ordinaryUnit.

proof.text: The existing integralScalarExtension_exact theorem proves finite-limit preservation for actual internal scalar extension. Transfer it to sectionwise extension through the ordinary extension comparison and the inverse encoding. Left adjoints preserve finite colimits. The encodings are additive since equivalences preserve binary products. Restriction retains its existing exactness instances.

For each fixed universal left-derived pair, compare it with the exact termwise functor using leftDerivedUnique and the canonical mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh. Its factorization identity is exactComparison_fac. Insert the quotient-to-derived isomorphisms and cancel their inverses to obtain exactComparison_complex on every cochain complex. Thus both actual derived pairs retain their specified counits. Transport the termwise shift structure and triangulated structure along the sectionwise comparison.

Localize the ordinary extension isomorphism with the existing mapDerivedCategorySquareIso. The composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations prove squareComplex. Whisker it with the two canonical universal-pair comparisons. Naturality and inverse cancellation prove exactly derivedExtensionComplex. The existing derived-equivalence instances for the two encodings give the required equivalences.

proof.text: Localize the ordinary cochain adjunction using the square determined by exactComparison_complex and the canonical exact restriction factorization. The explicit localization_unit_app formula, followed by inverse cancellation, is the required unit identity on every complex. This constructs the sectionwise adjunction directly and does not require a separate K-flat resolution argument.

source.place: Tag 04VG; localization of an exact adjunction

proof.text: For the specified actual internal adjunction, apply the already proved derived_unit_cochain identity from DerivedAdjointCochainCounit. This is the unit calculation underlying its public leftDerivedCochainCounit theorem. Unfold only reductionComplexCounit, remove the identity homotopy factor, and cancel the restriction factorization inverse. The resulting identity is internalUnit. Finally assemble the data and preserve the two ordinary section formulas established above.
